section_summary: This section covers State and War Department records from 1945 to 1949 concerning Japanese military commands, prisoner interrogation reports, and postwar occupation policies on disarmament and demobilization. It traces the transition from wartime military intelligence and psychological warfare considerations to Far Eastern Commission directives prohibiting military activity and destroying armaments. It concludes with high-level 1949 State Department debates over whether to reactivate Japanese armed forces or retain U.S. military bases in connection with the Japanese peace treaty.

subfiles.about: Reports German press announcements regarding Japanese Army Air Force command appointments.
subfiles.summary: Reports German press announcements that Japanese Army Air Force Commander-in-Chief Tojo was appointed Chief of General Staff and Yasuda appointed Commander.
subfiles.title: Appointment of Japanese Army Air Force Command

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Army reorganization and establishment of supreme commands for home defense and overseas areas.
subfiles.summary: Reports German press despatches detailing Japanese Army reorganization and appointment of supreme commanders for home defense forces and overseas armies.
subfiles.title: Japanese Army Reorganization and Supreme Commands

subfiles.about: Transmits Military Intelligence Service Report No. A-220 to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Cover memorandum forwarding Captured Personnel and Material Branch Report No. A-220 to the State Department liaison officer.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report on Captured Personnel

subfiles.about: Compiles statements by Japanese prisoners of war regarding morale, politics, war causes, the Emperor, and propaganda.
subfiles.from: P. E. Peabody (Military Intelligence Division, War Department)
subfiles.summary: Presents detailed statements from Japanese prisoners of war gathered in June 1945 concerning military morale, civilian hardship, and domestic politics. An officer and a student discuss war origins and comparative governance, strongly urging the preservation of the Imperial throne. A leading private outlines psychological warfare strategies and provides draft anti-suicide propaganda leaflets.
subfiles.title: Report No. A-220: Statements by Japanese Ps/W

subfiles.about: Requests guidance on War Department transmittal concerning Far Eastern Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip asking whether to comment or advise General McCoy regarding MacArthur's views on FEC paper SC-020/13.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip regarding Control of Japanese Military Activity

subfiles.about: Transmits General MacArthur's objections to a Soviet proposed amendment to FEC paper SC-020/13.
subfiles.from: Howard C. Petersen (Assistant Secretary of War)
subfiles.summary: Transmits General MacArthur's statements opposing a Soviet amendment on Japanese disarmament in FEC paper SC-020/13, arguing disarmament is already complete under U.S. directives.
subfiles.title: FEC Paper SC-020/13 and Disarmament of Japanese Armed Forces
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Outlines alternative U.S. positions regarding Soviet amendments to FEC paper SC-020/13.
subfiles.from: Lauris Norstad (Director of Plans & Operations, War Department)
subfiles.summary: Requests MacArthur's views on alternative U.S. courses of action regarding a Soviet proposed paragraph on disarmament in FEC paper SC-020/13.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Paper on Control of Japanese Military Activity in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence regarding Japanese soldiers allegedly holding out in Burma.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett (Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP censorship report of statements by repatriated lieutenant Masayoshi Ide alleging Japanese troops remain armed and hold out in Burma.
subfiles.title: Reported Japanese Army Holdouts in Burma

subfiles.about: Records designation of replacement copy for Tokyo Despatch No. 1330.
subfiles.summary: Official record replacement sheet indicating copy designated as permanent record copy replacing missing action copy of Tokyo Despatch 1330.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Slip for Despatch No. 1330

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1791 concerning reorganization and absorption of demobilization agencies.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAPIN 1791 directing transfer of First Demobilization Bureau to Welfare Ministry and elimination of Second Demobilization Bureau.
subfiles.title: Reorganization of Agencies Supervising Demobilization of Japanese Forces

subfiles.about: Inquires about conflicting Japanese demobilization figures in an article by George Atcheson, Jr.
subfiles.summary: Asks the State Department to clarify conflicting figures on Japanese military demobilization in George Atcheson Jr.'s article for 'Ten Eventful Years'.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Discrepancies in Japanese Demobilization Figures
subfiles.to: Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Provides official statistics and clarification on Japanese armed forces and demobilization.
subfiles.summary: Provides revised figures and an official statistical table from Jiji Nenkan detailing Japanese overseas army and navy personnel on August 15, 1945.
subfiles.title: Clarification of Japanese Demobilization Figures

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of clarified statistics regarding Japan's armed forces.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges with thanks Butterworth's letter providing updated information and figures concerning Japanese armed forces demobilization.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Demobilization Statistics

subfiles.about: Transmits certified copy of SCAP Directive Serial No. 89 to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman (Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Encloses certified copy of Directive Serial No. 89 regarding prohibition of military activity in Japan for the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of SCAP Directive Serial No. 89 to FEC

subfiles.about: Directs SCAP to prohibit Japanese military activity and dismantle military equipment and organizations.
subfiles.from: State, Army, Navy, and Air Force Departments
subfiles.summary: Sets forth comprehensive policy prohibiting Japanese military activity, arms manufacturing, aircraft production, and military organizations. Mandates seizure and destruction of military equipment, restricts police weaponry, confiscates military registration records, and bars former senior officers from public and educational positions.
subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 89: Prohibition of Military Activity in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of JCS Directive Serial No. 89 to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Forwards four copies of JCS Directive Serial No. 89 for transmittal to the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.
subfiles.title: Directive Transmitted to SCAP by Joint Chiefs of Staff

subfiles.about: Reports Soviet press criticism of the Far Eastern Commission's Japanese demilitarization decision.
subfiles.summary: Reports Tass article criticizing U.S. portrayal of Soviet abstention on FEC demilitarization decision and reviewing Soviet arguments regarding voting machinery.
subfiles.title: Soviet Criticism of FEC Demilitarization Decision

subfiles.about: Reports clarifying statements by Korean Foreign Minister Cho Pyong-ok regarding Japanese rearmament.
subfiles.summary: Encloses memorandum of conversation with Korean Foreign Minister Cho Pyong-ok, who denied alleging U.S. rearmament of Japan, explaining his press comments were purely hypothetical.
subfiles.title: Reported Statement of Korean Foreign Minister on Rearmament of Japan

subfiles.about: Reports Chinese broadcast alleging MacArthur approved KMT recruitment of Japanese troops.
subfiles.summary: Reports broadcast claiming MacArthur approved recruitment of 100,000 Japanese troops for China and recommends a timely official denial.
subfiles.title: Broadcast Allegations of Japanese Recruitment for China

subfiles.about: Analyzes policy alternatives regarding potential reactivation of Japanese armed forces in peace treaty planning.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes four alternative positions on reactivating Japanese armed forces in a peace treaty. Recommends deferring any decision to periodic five-year treaty reviews, highlighting General MacArthur's objections, Asian allies' fears of Japanese aggression, Japanese constitutional renunciation of war, and priority of war prevention over rearmament.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Reactivation of Japanese Armed Forces

subfiles.about: Provides personal comments on State Department memorandum regarding reactivation of Japanese forces and bases.
subfiles.from: Philip C. Jessup (US Mission to UN)
subfiles.summary: Jessup expresses strong opposition to Japanese rearmament, supporting MacArthur's emphasis on preventing war, and questions the long-term diplomatic impact of retaining U.S. military bases in Japan.
subfiles.title: Views on Reactivation of Japanese Armed Forces and Bases
